newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ung Huot says Cambodia ready for ASEAN mission.
newsitem.headline: Ung Huot says Cambodia ready for ASEAN mission.

text.p: Malaysian Foreign Minister Abdullah Badawi said on Tuesday he had received a letter from Cambodian Foreign Minister Ung Huot on behalf of strongman Hun Sen welcoming an ASEAN mediation mission to Phnom Penh.
Abdullah said the letter, dated July 29, had been faxed to Kuala Lumpur.
It was addressed to three ASEAN foreign ministers headed by Indonesia's Ali Alatas, mandated by the nine-member grouping to seek a solution to the Cambodian crisis.
Abdullah said he was confident of its authenticity as he had been told in a phone call from Phnom Penh on Monday to expect it.

The letter, which Ung Huot said was sent on behalf of Second Prime Minister Hun Sen and Cambodia, stated: "I have the pleasure to reconfirm that Cambodia welcomes ASEAN's role to help restore political stability to the country...
"I would like to invite you, Excellencies...to come to Cambodia at a date convenient to them, if possible this week."

Hun Sen had rebuffed an earlier mediation mission, led by Alatas and including the foreign ministers of Thailand and the Philippines, after he had ousted coalition partner and First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh in a bloody putsch in early July.

The Cambodia crisis topped the agenda during the annual meetings of foreign ministers of the Association of South East Asian Ministers (ASEAN) and with the ministers of major Asian and Western powers over the past week.
Cambodia had been due to join ASEAN last week along with Burma and Laos, but its membership was put on hold due to the political crisis there.
ASEAN, celebrating its 30th anniversary, currently comprises Brunei, Burma, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.

ASEAN, backed by the other participants including the United States, China, Japan, Russia and the European Union, offered to continue its mediation in Cambodia, but only after a clear-cut commitment from Hun Sen to welcome the mission.
The ministers had been confused by conflicting reports on Hun Sen's attitude issuing from Phnom Penh.
Asked when he expected to go to Phnom Penh, Alatas said he was returning to Jakarta later on Tuesday and would report to President Suharto.

"I cannot just go from here (Kuala Lumpur), and then I will have to coordinate about a date with the other two foreign ministers and with Phnom Penh. So when I get back to Jakarta, there will be a lot of phoning that I will have to do," he said with a chuckle.
Diplomatic sources said the ASEAN team was also expected to seek meetings with Cambodia's head of state, King Sihanouk, who is undergoing medical treatment in Beijing, and with Ranariddh.

Asked at an earlier news briefing about Sihanouk's role in the crisis, Philippines Foreign Minister Domingo Siazon said: "This is a game about three personalities essentially, not even parties, personalities and very important ones."
He quoted Sihanouk as having told the previous mediation mission that he felt like "a fish swimming between two rivers".
"Can you imagine that?" Siazon asked to laughter.
They met Sihanouk and Ranariddh on their earlier mediation shuttle and the two men accepted ASEAN mediation, which then foundered on Hun Sen's obduracy.

Alatas on Tuesday refused to reveal what approach his team would take to Hun Sen, saying this was a time for "quiet diplomacy" during which they expected to hear the Cambodian premier's views spelled out for the first time.

There was a general consensus during the ASEAN meetings that the Cambodian authorities must respect the 1991 Paris peace accords and the results of the 1993 general elections, adhere to principles of human rights and political freedoms, and guarantee free and fair elections in May next year.
